Why banks pay such
different interest

lines.text: Same $10,000. One bank pays $1. Another pays $400.
lines.say: Ten grand. One bank pays a dollar. Another pays four hundred.

lines.text: As of September 2026, some big banks paid 0.01% on savings. Top online banks paid about 4%.
lines.say: As of September twenty twenty-six, some big banks paid zero point zero one percent. Top online banks paid about four percent.

lines.text: On $10,000 for a year, that's $1 versus about $400.
lines.say: On ten thousand dollars for a year, that's one dollar versus about four hundred.

lines.text: The national average sits in between: 0.39% in January 2026, per the FDIC.
lines.say: The national average sits in between, at zero point three nine percent in January twenty twenty-six, per the FDIC.

lines.text: So why the gap? Branches, ATMs and staff cost money. Online banks skip most of that.
lines.say: So why the gap? Branches, ATMs and staff cost money. Online banks skip most of that.

lines.text: Big banks also have plenty of deposits, and many customers never shop around.

post.title: Why one bank pays $1 and another pays $400
post.ig:
Same $10,000. One bank pays you $1. Another pays $400.

As of September 2026, some big banks paid 0.01% APY on standard savings, while top online banks paid about 4%.
The FDIC national average was 0.39% in January 2026.
The gap: branch costs, plenty of deposits, and customers who don't shop around.

Sources: FDIC National Rates and Rate Caps, Bankrate, US News (Sept 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
